name: Grip strength
rangeNote: A fitness test, so there is no lab range: your result is compared with people of your age and sex in published norm tables (shown on this page).
summary: How hard you can squeeze a hand dynamometer, in kilograms. It is a quick measure of muscle strength that tracks strength in other parts of the body moderately well.

high.meaning: A stronger grip for your age and sex means more muscle strength, which goes with better health on average.

low.meaning: A weaker grip for your age and sex is linked, on average, with higher risk of disability and death in population studies. In older people it can be a first sign of muscle loss (sarcopenia), which a doctor can check.
commonCauses: A different device or way of measuring
